problemStatement.plain: Is Euler's number e = 2.71828... absolutely normal — does every finite digit string appear with the expected limiting frequency in every base?
whyMatters: No specific constant has ever been proved normal in any base — resolving this for e would be a landmark result
Borel (1909) proved almost all reals are absolutely normal but provides no examples
Computational evidence (5×10¹³ digits) is consistent with normality but cannot constitute proof

proven: First 6 decimal digits of e = 2.718281... proved from Mathlib bounds
Normal numbers must be irrational (necessary condition)
open: Whether e is normal in base 10
Whether e is normal in base 2
Whether ANY specific constant is normal in any base
knownResults.goal: Prove IsAbsolutelyNormal (Real.exp 1) — genuinely open as of 2026

insights: Mathlib's exp_one_gt_d9 (e>2.718281828) and exp_one_lt_d9 (e<2.7182818286) suffice to pin all 6 decimal digits
Int.floor_eq_iff.mpr + push_cast + linarith is the canonical pattern for floor lemmas about e
IsNormalInBase uses Tendsto with (b:ℝ)^(-(k:ℤ)) for the 1/bᵏ target — integer exponents handle negative powers
nthDigit uses ℤ return type to avoid subtraction issues; Fin b is used in string patterns
periodic_has_missing_ktuple and normal_imp_irrational axiomatized due to ℤ↔Fin b casting complexity in Tendsto setting
The open conjecture e_absolutely_normal mirrors the pattern from e-transcendental-oq-01 (schanuel_conjecture axiom)
mathlibGaps: No Mathlib lemma connecting ℤ-valued digit functions to Fin b sequences in Tendsto framework — blocks full proof of normal_imp_irrational
No Mathlib formalization of Borel's 1909 normality theorem
nextSteps: Consider proving periodic_has_missing_ktuple via Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn once the injectivity argument is worked out
Consider proving normal_imp_irrational fully by adding a bridge lemma connecting nthDigit ℤ values to Fin b
